chunks: Forty-three - Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us in Shawwal in the year one and eighty of the two hundredth century, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Tawil narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Sir, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, from al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding His Exalted Saying: {And those who disbelieve say, 'Why is not a sign sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.} He said: 'Every Imam is a guide for the generation in which he is.'

key_terms.وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ: And for every people is a guide

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'guide' mentioned in the Quranic verse 'And for every people is a guide'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq, the phrase 'for every people is a guide' (li-kulli qawmin hadin) is interpreted to mean that each generation (qarn) has its own specific Imam who serves as the spiritual guide for that era. This exegesis underscores the Shia doctrine of the continuous, unbroken line of Imams, ensuring that every community has a divinely appointed authority to guide them through their specific historical period. It reinforces the necessity of the Imam's presence in every age to preserve religious truth and provide guidance.
